make.name: MG
make.description: British sports-car marque founded in 1924 and owned by China's SAIC Motor since 2007. Today MG sells affordable electric cars worldwide (MG4, MGS5, MGS6, Cyberster), Indian-market EVs built on Wuling and Baojun designs (Comet, Windsor), and in Europe and Australia it also sells SAIC's premium IM models as MG IM5 and IM6.

logo.license: Public domain (Wikimedia Commons); trademark of SAIC Motor

models.name: ZS EV
models.description: Electric version of MG's ZS small SUV, launched in 2019 (EZS in China) and sold across Europe, the UK, India, Australia and Southeast Asia. It was withdrawn from the UK and Europe in early 2025, when the MGS5 EV replaced it and the second-generation ZS became petrol and hybrid only.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Original electric version of the ZS small SUV, launched in China as the EZS and in Europe in 2019 with a 44.5 kWh battery.

generations.name: Facelift
generations.description: Late-2021 facelift with a closed-off grille, new batteries (51.1 kWh LFP and 72.6 kWh NMC; 50.3 kWh in India) and up to 177 PS.

models.name: MG5 EV
models.description: Battery-electric estate car, a rebadged Roewe Ei5, sold in the UK and Europe from 2020 and in Thailand as the MG EP. MG stopped selling it in the UK and Europe in early 2025 and did not replace it; Chinese production of the Ei5 ended in 2025.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Export version of the Roewe Ei5 estate, sold in the UK from September 2020 and in Thailand as the MG EP.

generations.name: Facelift
generations.description: March 2022 facelift with a new nose and a 135 kW motor; withdrawn from the UK and Europe in early 2025 without a direct replacement, still sold in Thailand (MG EP / MG ES).

models.name: Marvel R Electric
models.description: Mid-size electric SUV sold in Europe from 2021, the export version of the Rising Auto Marvel R. It was MG's flagship EV in Europe until 2026; the MGS6 EV is its successor.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: European version of the Chinese R (Rising) Marvel R, launched in Europe in 2021.

models.name: MG4 EV
models.description: MG's compact electric hatchback and its best-selling EV in Europe, launched in 2022 (MG Mulan in China) with a high-performance XPower version. A second generation, front-drive and lighter, went on sale in China in 2025 and in the UK in 2026 as the MG4 EV Urban, alongside the older car.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Rear-drive hatchback launched in July 2022 (Mulan in China). Chinese production ended in 2025; export production continues, and the UK kept only the Extended Range and XPower after the second generation arrived.

generations.name: Second generation (MG4 Urban)
generations.description: All-new front-drive car on sale in China from September 2025 and in the UK from January 2026 as the MG4 EV Urban, about 150 kg lighter, with LFP or semi-solid-state batteries.

models.name: Cyberster
models.description: Two-seat electric roadster with scissor doors, revealed in 2023 for MG's centenary and sold in China, Europe, the UK and Australia. It is offered with a single rear motor or dual motors and a 64 or 77 kWh battery.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Two-seat electric roadster with scissor doors, built in Ningde, China, shown at Goodwood in July 2023.

models.name: MGS5 EV
models.description: Rear-drive electric compact SUV, sold in China as the MG ES5 from November 2024 and in the UK, Europe and Australia from 2025. It replaced the ZS EV (and, in effect, the MG5 EV estate) in the UK.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Rear-drive electric compact SUV launched in China as the MG ES5 in November 2024 and in the UK in April 2025.

models.name: MGS6 EV
models.description: Mid-size electric family SUV (a Skoda Enyaq rival) with a 77 kWh battery and rear- or all-wheel drive, launched in the UK at the end of 2025 and in continental Europe and Australia in 2026. It succeeds the Marvel R as MG's larger electric SUV in Europe.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Mid-size electric SUV derived from the Chinese SAIC H5, priced for the UK in November 2025 and on sale in Austria from February 2026.

models.name: Comet EV
models.description: Two-door, four-seat city car sold in India from April 2023, a rebadged Wuling Air EV.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Indian-market rebadge of the Wuling Air EV, assembled at Halol.

models.name: Windsor EV
models.description: Electric crossover hatchback sold in India from 2024, a rebadged Baojun Yunduo (also sold as the Wuling Cloud EV).

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Indian version of the Baojun Yunduo, assembled at Halol; the Pro with a 52.9 kWh pack was added in May 2025.

models.name: M9
models.description: Large electric luxury MPV sold in India through MG Select from July 2025; it is the Maxus Mifa 9 (LDV Mifa 9 in Australia) with MG badges.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Indian-market MG Select version of the Maxus Mifa 9 electric MPV, launched 21 July 2025.

images.credit: MG Select (JSW MG Motor India) press photo

models.name: MG 07
models.description: Mid-size electric (and plug-in hybrid) fastback sedan launched in China at the Chengdu show in August 2026 from about 105,900 yuan. It is 4,886 mm long; MG plans to bring it to Europe.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Fastback sedan launched in China in August 2026 with BEV and PHEV versions; the 845 version uses an 800 V CATL pack.

models.name: MG 4X
models.description: Compact electric crossover launched in China in 2026, built alongside the second-generation MG4 and offered with a semi-solid-state battery option.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Compact electric crossover (4,500 mm) that reached Chinese dealers in May 2026, offered with a semi-solid-state ('liquid-solid') battery.
